theme: Source adjudication of proposed lexical senses and dictionary compound boundaries
question: Which current lexical forms and sampled compound boundaries can be resolved directly from held dictionary and proposal sources?
outcome: Reviewed all 24 forms, 56 exact Tamil Lexicon records and 38 selected senses or contextual entries. Two cited alternatives were assigned the wrong language: āvu is Kannada/Telugu and tōḷ is Toda. Four source-attested form relations have limited contexts. Among 20 accepted splits in a frozen stratified Winslow sample, 17 have source-supported boundaries, 1 is wrong and 2 remain unresolved; among 20 rejected rows, 2 are documented missed compounds, 9 unresolved and 9 outside the declared two-noun or two-member scope. Three known failures were reviewed separately. A general source guard suppresses the false jamīṉ split and preserves parent origin marks. No reading effect was rerun.
challenge: Homographs, numeral combining forms, cross-language extraction mistakes and ambiguous morphology made form-only lookup insufficient. Row-origin flags omitted parent metadata, and dictionary crosschecks sometimes reused Winslow rather than adding independent attestation. The audit cannot supply dictionary-wide recall or verified earliest dates.
remedy: Froze a deterministic forty-row sample before reading source outcomes; bound every reviewed record to original source blocks and hashes; retained unresolved cases and separate regression rows; preserved source-specific language and sense choices; added a tested general grammatical-root guard without word-specific patches.
retry_when: A Dravidianist has reviewed unresolved member identities, historical senses and noun eligibility, and a complete versioned extraction with general increment handling can be evaluated on an independently adjudicated sample.

authors.model: GPT-6; exact backend identifier not exposed
